title: Omurice
subtitle: thin omelette wrapped around savoury fried rice
excerpt: Omurice is a Japanese comfort dish of ketchup-seasoned chicken fried rice wrapped in a thin, golden egg omelette. It is a beloved yoshoku dish that children and adults alike order at family restaurants. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Omurice is a Japanese invention from the early twentieth century, combining the French omelette technique with rice, creating one of Japan's most popular yoshoku dishes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice and chicken filling up to 1 day ahead. Make the omelette fresh to order.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fried rice seasoned with ketchup, soy sauce, and mirin, used as the filling for omurice. The ketchup gives it a slightly sweet, tangy flavour.
A popular restaurant-style omurice where a soft, barely-set omelette is placed on top of the rice and sliced open to drape over it, rather than wrapping the rice.

content.text: filling and a thin egg omelette that wraps around it. The classic shape is a neat oval. The
style with a soft, split omelette draping over the rice is a slightly easier alternative. Serves 4.
Use day-old rice if possible. Freshly cooked rice is too moist for frying and tends to clump rather than stay separate.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Add the cold rice. Break up any clumps and stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add soy sauce, mirin, and peas. Toss to combine. Taste and adjust. Divide the fried rice into 4 equal portions and keep warm.
Beat 2 eggs for the first omelette. Heat a small knob of butter in the 26 cm pan over medium-high heat until foaming.
Pour in the beaten eggs. Swirl the pan so the egg covers the base evenly. Cook for 30 to 40 seconds until the edge is set but the centre is still slightly wet.

Place one portion of rice in the centre of the omelette. Fold both sides over the rice and flip onto a plate seam-side down. Shape into an oval with a folded cloth or paper. Repeat for the remaining 3 portions.

attrs.cause: The egg layer was too thin or the rice filling was piled too high.
attrs.fix: Use 2 eggs per portion and keep the rice mound compact and slightly domed in the centre of the omelette.

attrs.symptom: Fried rice is sticky and clumping
attrs.cause: Freshly cooked rice was used or it was too wet.
attrs.fix: Spread cooked rice on a tray and refrigerate uncovered for at least 1 hour before frying.

attrs.symptom: Omelette is browned rather than pale yellow
attrs.cause: The heat was too high or the pan was not fully coated with butter.
attrs.fix: Keep heat at medium-high, not high, and make sure butter coats the pan completely before adding eggs.

content.text: Omurice is a fixture on the menus of Japan's yoshoku family restaurants. Children ask for it by name. Cooks have competed for decades over the perfect omelette wrap technique. The demi style, where a soft egg is split and draped, became famous after a Tokyo restaurant video went viral. Both styles taste the same. The wrapping is just a matter of pride.
